history.message: You enter the library.
Robner lies on the Library floor beside a teacup and a saucer. The preliminary estimate places his death at about 8 p.m. on July 7, 1982.
The overturned, hand-painted cup has a brown mark at the bottom and smells faintly of tea.
Robner's clothing holds no additional clue in this case.
The overturned saucer is hand-painted with a mythological scene and has small brown marks. It smells faintly of tea and matches the household service.
The bottle is labeled for Marshall Robner. Its 25 mg Ebullion tablets are prescribed for depression: one or two twice daily. The label warns that a sufficient dosage may be harmful or fatal.
The desk is orderly except for a blank-looking notepad.
The desk drawers contain no further evidence.
The page looks blank, but shallow pressure marks remain in the paper.
Shading the page reveals impressions left by writing on the previous sheet. The writer pressed hard, but only fragments are legible: ‘Baxter,’ ‘merg...,’ ‘Omnidyne,’ ‘Focus,’ and ‘recons...’.
The books are carefully arranged. One section is slightly out of line.
Behind the shifted books you find a concealed safe.
Inside the safe are two documents: a packet of papers and a new will.

Focus Corporation was a subsidiary of Robner Corp. These papers document funds Baxter embezzled from Focus and describe how the scandal was hushed up. Robner's records describe how the matter was handled.
The new will disinherits George and leaves Robner's entire estate to his wife.
The cup contains a trace of tea. Its fingerprints are Robner's.
The saucer contains traces of tea and sugar. Its fingerprints are Robner's and Dunbar's.

“Baxter and I attended the concert. He was with me, and he took me home after it ended.”
The private interview with Dunbar ends. Dunbar returns to the officer and the group.
You enter the kitchen.
There are eight large and small plates, seven saucers, and six cups.
You enter the garden.
There are two holes in the soft earth, each about two inches by four inches and at least three inches deep. The soil around them is compacted.
Digging in the soft earth, you cut your finger on a sharp edge and find a piece of porcelain covered in dirt and dried mud.
As you wipe off the porcelain, its hand-painted design becomes visible.
The lab finds traces of tea and sugar, along with another chemical not commonly used as medication. It is not Amitraxin (Ebullion). No clear fingerprints remain.

The lab finds Methsparin, the active ingredient in LoBlo, on the fragment and at a high level in Robner's blood. Methsparin can displace Ebullion from proteins in the blood, leaving more free Ebullion there. The pathologist concludes that the combination caused fatal Ebullion toxicity.
You enter the living room.

terminal.title: Accusation on record
terminal.message: The case record now names Baxter and Dunbar. Close the case on these accusations, or continue investigating.

pendingMessages.message: The officer tells you a letter arrived while you were away. He left it on the table for you.

outcome.title: Case solved
outcome.message: The prosecution presents the poison report, Dunbar's possession of LoBlo, the adjacent concert ticket stubs timed to Robner's death, the conflicting accounts of how Dunbar left the concert, and the Focus papers and notepad impression linking Baxter to Robner's business dispute. The jury convicts Baxter and Dunbar of Robner's murder. The case is closed with both roles established by the evidence.
